newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen to sell 11 percent stake in LNG project.
newsitem.headline: Yemen to sell 11 percent stake in LNG project.

text.p: Yemen is planning to sell an 11 percent stake in the Yemen Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) Company, retaining a share of only 15 percent, Yemen's minister of oil and mineral resources said in remarks published on Thursday.
"We intend to hold on to 15 percent and we'll sell the rest," Mohammad Said al-Attar, who is also deputy prime minister, was quoted as saying by the official daily al-Thawra.
"There are discussions with companies (about the sale) and in fact some of them have made several proposals," he said, but gave no further details.
Yemen signed a deal with foreign companies on Sunday firming the equity structure of the $5 billion LNG project which is expected to start exports by the year 2001.

Under the deal, France's Total SA took a 36 percent stake in the Yemen LNG Company, U.S. Exxon Corp jointly with Hunt Oil received 30 percent, South Korea's Yukong eight percent and Yemen's government 26 percent.
